Every decision about the film is made here BEFORE the build: builders build ONLY what this file says; anything missing is a bible change (LEAD edits, re-validates, logs it in CHANGES). Times are the linter's estimates (est_t0, briefs/v3/pointing/lint.json) until the voice is locked; after the lock the scaffold maps starts_on words to frames. Camera speeds were measured with CORE's camSpeedStats on the planned presets (tools/v3/cam_speed.mjs --plan; result in briefs/v3/pointing/cam_plan.json). Plain-words companion: briefs/v3/pointing/BIBLE_NOTES.md. Names: kit names that exist are used as they are; 'new': true = a kit request (see kit_requests), 'local': true / local/<name> = built inside videos3/pointing/sets/.

characters.speaker: DRIVER
characters.voice: cast 3 candidates (calm, crisp, firm adult male, 35-50; NO Japanese accent on the English words), 4+ takes per call-out, pick by clarity + timbre distance from James (LESSONS 51)
characters.delivery: each call-out is two beats: the NAME on a firm mid pitch, a held ~0.35-0.45 s beat (the hand goes to his ear), the STATUS short and clipped, a little louder: 'Signal... GREEN!'. Never shouted hoarse; crisp like a checklist. Payoff 'Doors... closed!' identical in rhythm to the plant (reuse the same take if it is the best)

characters.voice: cast 3 candidates (New Yorker, 20s, loud and cheerful, a REAL laugh); never mean
characters.delivery: 'Bro's pointing at nothing!' = laughing through it (the laugh starts on 'Bro's', a 0.3 s laugh tail after 'nothing!'); 'Stay. Be right back.' = to a dog, warm; 'Nobody does that in New York!' = proud, a grin you can hear; 'Vending machine... check!' = a stiff mock of the driver's rhythm; 'What's a finger gonna do, bro?' = grinning into the phone; 'Bag... gone.' = small, flat, deadpan, after a beat (the sharp contrast to the driver's crisp call)

gaps._doc: A2 (PIPELINE_V3): the pauses the PICTURE needs, decided here so the voice never changes after Gate 1. word = the same key as starts_on (the bare word, '#n' = its n-th occurrence in the whole voice). min_gap_s = the minimum silence from the END of this word to the START of the next spoken word (natural gap included). The voice lead inserts only the difference with tools/insert_pause.py. E = essential (the picture fails without it), N = nice (keep if the take has it; drop first if the film runs long).

gaps._lead_in: frame 0 is mid-snap: the driver's 'Signal' starts within 2 f of frame 0 (the glove-snap sfx at f0) so the loop from 'gone.' lands on the shout
gaps._projection: added silence beyond the natural ~0.25 s sentence gap: E gaps +5.2 s, N gaps +1.35 s. On the linter model (2.67 w/s) the shots add up to 73.9 s (est_dur_with_gaps_s per shot); the real James pace (2.8-3.0 w/s, SCRIPT v2: 3-5 s shorter) gives ~68.5 s with E only and ~70 s with E + N (0.8 s tail included). The script estimated only ~3 s of holds (61-66 s): this plan is ~3 s longer because the call-out montage, the tunnel gag and the payoff each need ~2 s on screen. If the assembled voice passes 70 s: drop the N gaps, then SCRIPT 5.2's cut order. Never time-stretch.

fact_guards: Japanese conventional lines: 1,067 mm narrow gauge; trains run on the LEFT track; the driver sits on the LEFT of the cab; lineside signals stand on the left of the track. No Shinkansen anything (the panel's red flag 1).
Door order is real: doors close -> the car-side pilot lamps go out -> the cab's all-doors-closed lamp lights -> the driver confirms (JTSB RI2015-3-1e). The car-side lamps glow while doors are open.
The calls are DRAMATIZED in English: real calls are Japanese and name the aspect (e.g. 'shinko', proceed), not the colour. The description says 'dramatized'.

New York: the zebra board is mid-platform, facing the train, opposite the conductor's window; he points at it before opening the doors; no board seen = no doors (Wikipedia F4; MTA via popular sources).
The lab task is DRAMATIZED: the sources say only 'a simple task' (RTRI 1994); never say what the task was. 6 vs 1 = 2.38 vs 0.38 per 100 actions. Never '85 % of drivers', never a crash number.
Over a thousand people: a packed 10-11-car Tokyo commuter train (E235 11-car set rated 1,628). We never show a car count.
Not claimed in picture either: who invented it, how old it is, that NY conductors call out loud.
culture_guards: No eating or drinking on the commuter train (no noodles, no ekiben, no boxed lunch). No makeup gag. No phone calls in the car.
NO Japanese text anywhere (pictograms, digits and arrows only). No JR / MTA / any logos; a plain 'NEW YORK' T-shirt; no route letters, no kana car numbers, no brands on the vending machine.
The tourist is likeable and dumb: he laughs, he gives the driver a thumbs-up, he is never rude to staff; the joke is on him, not on Japan.
Commuters are polite and quiet; the late salaryman does NOT rush the closing doors (kakekomi is bad manners): he stops and gives up.

Every framing in the call-out montage and the payoff holds >= ~2 s on screen with the voice gaps; no whips anywhere; medium or wide framings; the bag in the doorway and the 6 vs 1 jars readable at phone size.
Music never uses a Japanese pastiche (koto / shamisen / gong); the platform melody is our own original.
